subject.title: refactor(qqbot): install plugin from Tencent package

question: Should OpenClaw officially replace the bundled QQBot implementation with Tencent Connect’s external package before it has SecretRef parity, a proven in-place upgrade path, and equivalent security scanning ownership?
rationale: This changes the trusted code owner, executable package source, credential compatibility, and vulnerability-remediation boundary; those tradeoffs require explicit QQBot owner and security intent rather than an automated patch judgment.

options.title: Require parity before handoff
options.body: Keep the PR open until the external package supports the shipped credential contract, upgrade migration, documentation, and security review for the exact artifact.

options.title: Approve a documented breaking handoff
options.body: Explicitly accept the credential and operator migration, but require tested doctor guidance, release communication, and security approval before merge.

options.title: Keep QQBot bundled for now
options.body: Pause or close this handoff and retain the bundled implementation until Tencent’s package and ownership processes meet the repository’s compatibility and security bar.

recommendation.title: Require parity before handoff
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until the external package supports the shipped credential contract, upgrade migration, documentation, and security review for the exact artifact.

likelyOwner.reason: Sliverp is the strongest available QQBot feature and ownership-routing candidate, with security approval still required for the artifact boundary.
